Recent observations reinforce this: early-to-mid August saw frequent readings above 33°C at stations including Changi, with a peak of 34.9°C at Pulau Ubin on August 14 amid below-average rainfall and persistent southwest monsoon flow. These conditions—light southeasterly winds, high humidity, and limited convective cooling—have sustained elevated surface temperatures close to or above seasonal normals (August average high ~31.4°C). 

Forecast guidance for the 25th clusters around 31–34°C depending on the model and exact station, with some runs showing afternoon thunderstorm potential that could limit peaks while others favor clearer skies allowing brief 34°C spikes. The market's heavy weighting toward 33°C (over 50% implied probability) versus lower odds for 34°C or 32°C reflects this narrow consensus range, tempered by the inherent uncertainty in short-range tropical convection timing and localized heating. eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple meteorological sources indicate a high around 31–33°C for Beijing on August 25, 2026, driven by persistent warm, humid conditions from a regional high-pressure ridge combined with increasing cloud cover and thunderstorm activity.
